reading.title: How to Build a Strong Report
reading.purpose: Follow the steps writers use to gather facts, plan a draft, and polish their work.
paras: Writing a class report is much easier when you break it into clear steps. Each step has its own job, from finding facts to fixing small mistakes at the end.

Start by choosing a topic and asking what you already recall, or remember from earlier reading. Next, go to the library to locate useful books and gather notes in one folder. Read closely so you can identify the key facts and name what matters most.

Once your folder is full, you will have more notes than you need. Rank your facts from most important to least important, then select only the best details for your paper. Now outline your report by listing its main parts in order before you write full sentences.

As you draft, combine short, choppy ideas into smooth sentences. Do not stop after the first draft! Read it aloud and revise any part that sounds unclear, changing words to make it stronger. Last, edit your pages to fix spelling, capital letters, and periods.
When you follow these steps, a big writing job feels calm and doable.

choices: to fix spelling errors and missing periods
to plan writing by listing its main parts
to choose a brand-new topic at the library
to join two short sentences into one line
qs.why: Paragraph 3 explains that you outline your report "by listing its main parts in order before you write full sentences."

qs.q: Which sentence tells what a writer does during the last step?
choices: As you draft, combine short, choppy ideas into smooth sentences.
Do not stop after the first draft!
Last, edit your pages to fix spelling, capital letters, and periods.
When you follow these steps, a big writing job feels calm and doable.
qs.why: This sentence names editing spelling, capital letters, and periods as the final step.

ev.text: Last, edit your pages to fix spelling, capital letters, and periods.

qs.q: Why should a writer rank facts before selecting them?
choices: Ranking helps the writer keep the best facts and leave out weak ones.
Ranking makes the folder heavier so it is easier to locate at school.
Ranking fixes every spelling mistake before the writer writes a draft.
Ranking lets the writer use every single note without cutting anything.
qs.why: Paragraph 3 says you have more notes than you need, so ranking from most to least important helps you pick only the best details.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: Library books are always better than notes you already remember on your own in class.
Clear steps make planning, writing, and fixing a report easier.
Short sentences are always wrong and should never appear in a school report.
Fixing spelling and periods is the only step that makes a paper strong.
qs.why: The passage walks through each stage of writing a report and explains how those steps make the job manageable.
